title: A tiny eval harness: deterministic checks and a pass rate
goal: Finish an eval harness that scores a folder of saved agent outputs against a spec. Implement the deterministic checks (file exists, file contains, diff touches only allowed paths, diff size) so that they fail closed, then build the pass-rate report. No model calls: the judge-style check is reported as skipped, never as a pass.
setup_cmd: D=~/fm-ex/ex-5-4-evals-metrics; if [ -e "$D" ]; then echo "Already set up at $D. Run: cd $D (or delete it first to start over)."; else mkdir -p ~/fm-ex && cp -r exercises/ex-5-4-evals-metrics/starter "$D" && cd "$D" && git init -q -b main && git add -A && git -c user.name=fm-learner -c user.email=learner@example.com commit -q -m baseline && npm install; fi

starter_prompts.claude: Read AGENTS.md, src/checks.js, src/report.js and tests/harness.test.js. The harness is naive on purpose: it passes everything. Implement runCheck in src/checks.js and evaluateCase and buildReport in src/report.js so that npm test passes. Never edit tests/, outputs/ or evals/. Before you code, list the situations where a check should fail instead of pass (a missing file, a path that leaves the case folder, an empty diff, a .. segment in a diff path, an unknown check type) and tell me why a rubric check must never count as a pass. Then run npm test and node bin/run-evals.js and read the report.

Implement runCheck in src/checks.js and evaluateCase and buildReport in src/report.js so that npm test passes. Never edit tests/, outputs/ or evals/. Before you code, list the situations where a check should fail instead of pass (a missing file, a path that leaves the case folder, an empty diff, a .. segment in a diff path, an unknown check type) and tell me why a rubric check must never count as a pass. Then run npm test and node bin/run-evals.js and read the report.

solution_notes: Every doubtful situation is a failure: a missing file, a path that leaves the case folder (including through a symlink), an empty or missing diff, a bad regex, a bad limit and an unknown check type. file_not_contains on a missing file fails too, because a file that is not there cannot prove a pattern is absent.

diff_touches_only rejects any path with a '..' segment before it looks at the allow list, and it counts both sides of a rename. Otherwise 'src/../.github/workflows/ci.yml' would match 'src/**' and a rename out of a protected folder would look harmless.

A rubric check is 'skipped', not 'pass'. A case with nothing left to score is 'unscored' and stays out of the pass rate, so the number never includes a verdict that no judge gave. Deterministic checks decide first; a judge is only for what code cannot check.

The pass rate is over scored cases, rounded to three decimals, and it is null when nothing was scored. 'ok' needs a real rate at or above the threshold, so an empty or unscored run blocks instead of passing. evaluateCase never throws: a check that crashes is a failed check, so one bad case cannot hide the others.
